//: Committed baseline boot config. Safe to commit: it carries NO secrets. The DB
//secrets: 'database.password' is injected at deploy time from PZ_PG_PASSWORD
//secrets2: (script/utils.py -> script/start.py); the admin login lives hashed in the
//secrets3: local_users table (engined seeds a default and applies changes), NOT here;
//secrets4: SNMP v3 and vendor API credentials are entered via the web UI at runtime and
//secrets5: held sealed in their own tables, never in this document.
//shape: Three scopes, and the split is about ownership rather than about processes:
//shape2: global      infrastructure every daemon shares. Not operator-facing.
//shape3: pretzel     the appliance, addressed by DOMAIN - what is being configured,
//shape4: not which daemon happens to read it. Which one does is a fact
//shape5: about the code, and it has already changed twice (probed to
//shape6: collectord, inferd to pretzel-ai) without one operator's intent
//shape7: changing with it. Each of those moved config nobody had edited.
//shape8: pretzel-ai  the assistant, a separate service reached over gRPC. Its own
//shape9: scope because it deploys and versions on its own clock.
//derived: What is NOT here, deliberately: daemon_name, and per-daemon logger name and
//derived2: file. They were nine copies of one sentence, each derivable from the daemon's
//derived3: own name, and every copy a place for a typo to become a daemon logging to the
//derived4: wrong file. shared/core/Core.cpp derives all three from the name it already has.
//tuning: Internal tuning (heartbeat, bootstrap, probe batching, scan timeouts) is not
//tuning2: here either - each daemon reads it via config.value(key, <compiled default>),
//tuning3: so it is owned by the code defaults and never surfaces in the settings UI.
//assistant: pretzel-ai ships with NO providers. A provider exists because an operator added
//assistant2: one: it is a vendor they hold an account with, a key only they have, and the
//assistant3: models that account is entitled to. A factory baseline cannot know any of the
//assistant4: three, and one that guessed would show a configuration nobody made.
//assistant5: An entry is { id, models[] } and nothing else. The endpoint is not configuration -
//assistant6: it is a fact about the vendor, compiled in on the pretzel-ai side, so an operator
//assistant7: cannot point 'openai' at something that is not OpenAI. The API key is not here
//assistant8: either: it is sealed in ai_gateway_credential_state under the provider's own id.
